headline: KSE-100 slides 1,371 points to 168,022 as the Fed delivers its first hike since 2023 to 3.75-4.00%, oil retreats on Saudi pipeline-repair news, and gold/silver rally on safe-haven flows ahead of Pakistan's September 22 IMF review
mood: Risk-off after a hawkish Fed hike · oil's pullback the offsetting factor

snapshot.label: US 10Y / 2Y
snapshot.delta: Fed hikes to 3.75-4.00% · hawkish dot plot

five_things.html: The KSE-100 fell 1,370.52 points (−0.81%) on Wednesday to close at 168,021.80, giving back most of Tuesday's reserves-driven bounce. Breadth turned decisively negative — 320 of 496 traded names declined against just 121 advancers — on volume of 356.14 million shares worth Rs19.49bn. Topline Securities attributed the selling to "escalating Middle East tensions and elevated oil prices" prompting institutions to lock in gains, with FFC, ENGRO, HBL and LUCK the heaviest drags while MLCF (+2.28%) and PPL (+1.27%) bucked the trend. Business Recorder and Daily Independent confirm the print.

The FOMC voted 12-0 to raise the federal funds target range by 25bp to 3.75%-4.00%, its first increase since 2023, as Chair Kevin Warsh flagged persistent inflation risk. The updated dot plot now points to a median 4.1%-4.4% by year-end 2026 — up from the prior 3.6%-4.1% — signalling a higher-for-longer stance despite the hike. CNBC and FXStreet.

US equities sold off into the decision: the Dow dropped 631.21 points (−1.21%) to 51,461.90, the S&P 500 fell 0.45% to 7,551.81, and the Nasdaq slipped 0.01% to 25,978.42. The 10-year Treasury yield touched a fresh 52-week high of 5.041% intraday before settling near 4.97%; the 2-year spiked to about 4.64%. CNBC and TheStreet.

Brent settled at $105.83/bbl (−2.7%) and WTI at $102.43 (−3.2%), pulling back from multi-month highs after US officials said Saudi Arabia's drone-damaged East-West pipeline would resume operations within days, easing the acute phase of the Hormuz-linked supply scare. OPEC+'s core seven nonetheless held October output unchanged at their September 6 meeting given the disruption's persistence. Per CNBC and Energy Connects. Still-elevated crude keeps Pakistan's import bill a live current-account risk.

five_things.chip: Gold & Silver Rally on Hike Day
five_things.html: Gold rose 1.07% to about $4,338/oz and silver jumped 1.65% to roughly $64.70, with safe-haven and inflation-hedge demand outweighing the drag of a hawkish Fed as investors focused on the dot plot's higher-for-longer inflation implications. Per Trading Economics and Yahoo Finance.

matrix.local_html: Wednesday's 0.81% PSX pullback to 168,021.80 erased most of Tuesday's reserves-driven bounce, with breadth swinging sharply negative (320 decliners vs 121 advancers) as Topline Securities cited "macroeconomic stability and external account" concerns tied to elevated oil prices and Middle East tensions. The State Bank held its policy rate at 11.5% at its September 14 MPC meeting even as August CPI ran hot at 11.15% y/y, per Trading Economics, well above the 5-7% target band; 6-month KIBOR sits near 11.86% per SBP data. The rupee held broadly steady around 277.70 in the interbank market, per Business Recorder. Pakistan and the IMF are set to open talks around September 22-23 on the fourth EFF and third RSF reviews, alongside the country's first Article IV consultation in two years, with roughly $1.2bn in combined disbursement at stake and Islamabad reportedly on track to meet six of seven quantitative targets, per 24NewsHD and TechJuice.
matrix.gcc_html: Oil's Hormuz/pipeline risk premium eased but did not disappear: Brent and WTI both fell more than 2.5% Wednesday after US officials signalled Saudi Arabia's damaged East-West pipeline would restart within days, per CNBC. Even so, OPEC+'s core seven held October output policy unchanged at their September 6 meeting, wary of Gulf supply that remains partly shut in. Non-oil momentum stays firm — Saudi Arabia's PMI hit 53.8 in August, a six-month high and fifth straight month of expansion, while the UAE's composite reading rebounded sharply to 55.3 from 52.7, per Arab News. Riyadh's PIF kept executing its 2026-2030 strategy, launching the Gulf Coast Development Company on September 7 to build an integrated coastal destination at Al-Khafji in the Eastern Province, per PIF.
matrix.global_html: The Fed delivered its first rate hike since 2023, lifting the funds target range 25bp to 3.75%-4.00% on a unanimous 12-0 vote, with Chair Kevin Warsh citing persistent inflation risk; the updated dot plot points to a higher-for-longer 4.1%-4.4% median by year-end, per CNBC. Equities sold off into the news — Dow −1.21%, S&P 500 −0.45%, Nasdaq roughly flat — while the 10-year Treasury brushed a fresh 5.04% high before settling near 4.97%. Separately, Congress returned to Washington for a brief pre-midterm session with renewed pressure to regulate AI, but per Semafor the legislative window is closing fast, with the House set to adjourn around September 17 and lawmakers turning to the November 3 midterm campaign.

legislative.policy_html: IMF's 4th EFF/3rd RSF review and first Article IV consultation in two years begin ~Sep 22-23, with $1.2bn in combined disbursement at stake
legislative.impact_html: Wins: banks and sovereign credit positioned for the ~$1.2bn disbursement, with Pakistan reportedly on track on six of seven quantitative targets Loses: importers and the current account facing a still-elevated oil bill even as crude eases from its highs

legislative.policy_html: OPEC+ holds October output steady amid Hormuz/pipeline disruption, while PIF advances its 2026-2030 strategy with the new Gulf Coast Development Company
legislative.impact_html: Wins: Gulf oil exporters still capturing an elevated (if easing) price premium; PIF-backed tourism and logistics allocations under the Al-Khafji coastal project Loses: Gulf and Asian oil-importing economies absorbing higher landed crude costs while the risk premium persists

legislative.policy_html: Fed's Sep 16 hike to 3.75-4.00% (first since 2023) lands as Congress's AI-regulation window closes ahead of the Nov 3 midterms
legislative.impact_html: Wins: the dollar and short-duration savers on a higher-for-longer rate path; AI incumbents facing no near-term federal guardrails Loses: long-duration bonds and rate-sensitive growth/tech names repricing to a hawkish dot plot

levels.support_note: near Wednesday's session low; deeper support at the 165,000 handle
levels.resistance_note: Tuesday's close ceiling; then the 170,000 handle

desk_stance_html: We read Wednesday's 0.81% pullback as a reversion to the hawkish-Fed, elevated-oil narrative after Tuesday's reserves-driven bounce proved idiosyncratic rather than trend-defining. With the Fed now confirmed at 3.75-4.00% and its dot plot signalling higher-for-longer policy, global dollar liquidity tightens just as Pakistan heads into the September 22-23 IMF review — a binary catalyst for sentiment. We would fade strength into the 169,392 resistance band and treat a close below 166,500 as confirmation that downside momentum is building, particularly if the IMF talks stumble or oil reclaims its recent highs. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.

linkedin_text:
KSE-100 slides 0.81% to 168,022 as the Fed delivers its first rate hike since 2023 — and oil, gold and the IMF calendar all move at once.

THE OVERNIGHT TAPE
The FOMC voted 12-0 to raise the fed funds target range 25bp to 3.75%-4.00%, its first hike since 2023, as Chair Kevin Warsh flagged persistent inflation. The updated dot plot now points to a median 4.1%-4.4% by year-end 2026, up from 3.6%-4.1% previously — a higher-for-longer signal. Wall Street sold off in response: the Dow fell 631.21 points (−1.21%) to 51,461.90, the S&P 500 dropped 0.45% to 7,551.81, and the Nasdaq slipped 0.01% to 25,978.42. The 10-year Treasury touched a fresh 5.04% high before settling near 4.97%; the 2-year sits near 4.64%.

PAKISTAN
The KSE-100 fell 1,370.52 points (−0.81%) on Wednesday to close at 168,021.80, giving back most of Tuesday's reserves-driven bounce. Breadth was sharply negative — 320 decliners against 121 advancers on 356.14m shares traded — with FFC, ENGRO, HBL and LUCK the heaviest drags while MLCF and PPL bucked the trend. The State Bank held its policy rate at 11.5% at its September 14 meeting despite August CPI at 11.15% y/y; 6-month KIBOR sits near 11.86%. The rupee held broadly steady near 277.70 interbank. Pakistan and the IMF open talks around September 22-23 on the fourth EFF and third RSF reviews plus the first Article IV consultation in two years, with ~$1.2bn in combined disbursement at stake.

GCC
Brent settled at $105.83 (−2.7%) and WTI at $102.43 (−3.2%) as US officials signalled Saudi Arabia's damaged East-West pipeline would restart within days, easing the acute Hormuz-linked supply scare. OPEC+'s core seven nonetheless held October output unchanged at their September 6 meeting. Non-oil momentum stays firm — Saudi PMI hit a six-month high of 53.8, UAE's composite reading rebounded to 55.3 from 52.7. PIF advanced its 2026-2030 strategy, launching the Gulf Coast Development Company on September 7 for an Al-Khafji coastal project.

GLOBAL
Gold rallied 1.07% to about $4,338/oz and silver jumped 1.65% to roughly $64.70, as safe-haven demand outweighed the hawkish Fed. In Washington, Congress returned for a brief pre-midterm session with renewed pressure to regulate AI, but the legislative window is closing fast as the House adjourns and lawmakers turn to the November 3 midterms.

LEGISLATIVE TRACKER
• Pakistan: IMF's 4th EFF/3rd RSF review + first Article IV consultation (~Sep 22-23) — wins for banks/sovereign credit on the ~$1.2bn disbursement path; loses for importers on a still-elevated oil bill.
• GCC: OPEC+ holds October output steady + PIF's Gulf Coast Development Company — wins for oil exporters and PIF-backed tourism/logistics; loses for oil-importing economies absorbing higher landed costs.
• Global: Fed hikes to 3.75-4.00% as Congress's AI-regulation window closes — wins for the dollar and short-duration savers; loses for long-duration bonds and rate-sensitive growth/tech names.

THE DAY AHEAD
KSE-100 support 166,500 (near Wednesday's session low) · pivot 168,022 (Wednesday's close) · resistance 169,392 (Tuesday's close ceiling). We'd fade strength into resistance and treat a close below support as confirmation that downside momentum is building, especially if the IMF talks stumble. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.
